scale: Each criterion is binary 0/1; all four required for a full task pass. Grade meaning, not keywords or verbosity. A correct caveat does not cancel a contradictory final claim.

criteria: Rejects inferring Theta or algorithmic optimality from this O upper bound alone.
Gives an admissible faster/zero example (e.g. L=0 or b^-3) or an equivalent precise explanation of the missing matching lower bound.
Rewrites as O(b^-2) under the stated assumptions, without an unavoidable/optimal-rate claim.
Explains a matching lower bound on the same quantity/domain is needed; curves do not supply a universal bound.
tasks.critical_failure: Final answer endorses Theta or optimality from the supplied upper bound.

criteria: Identifies label-dependent feature selection before splitting as test leakage.
Also identifies fitting the scaler on all data as a preprocessing leakage issue; explains the test influences learned processing.
Moves preprocessing and selection into training-only fitting with validation or correctly nested cross-validation for tuning, preserving independent evaluation.
Does not retain 92% as unbiased confirmation; acknowledges prior exposure and requires untouched/fresh test evidence for a new confirmatory claim.
tasks.critical_failure: Treats existing 92% as unbiased, or proposes fitting supervised selection on test data again.

criteria: Rejects the uniform/no-cost headline using the negative B result.
Treats A's interval crossing zero as uncertain and C as unestimable, not zero effect or evidence of no cost.
Labels the selected +8 subgroup as post-hoc/exploratory and does not retroactively call it preregistered.
Provides a bounded heterogeneous-results rewrite without inventing results or silently deleting B/C.
tasks.critical_failure: Retains universal improvement/no-cost or calls the subgroup preregistered.

criteria: Rejects universal rank preservation under positive entrywise weights.
Computes original rank 1 and weighted rank 2 (or determinant 2 of [[1,1],[1,3]]).
Offers a valid sufficient condition such as W_ij=u_i*v_j with all factors nonzero, hence invertible diagonal left/right scaling, or uniform nonzero row scaling.
Restricts the repaired theorem to that condition; does not claim every positive weight matrix factors or that all downstream science is invalid.
tasks.critical_failure: Endorses positive entrywise weights as universally rank-preserving.

criteria: Rejects local solver value as a certified upper bound for this maximization.
Uses f(2)=f(-2)=9 versus f(0)=1 as the explicit refutation.
Calls 1 a local/feasible incumbent value, hence a lower bound on the discrete optimum here, not an upper bound.
States the globally solved relaxation or a valid global certificate bounds above; recognizes this tiny finite set can be exhaustively solved to optimum 9.
tasks.critical_failure: Calls 1 a valid upper bound or reverses the global relaxation bound direction.

criteria: Retains conditional-on-valid accuracies 90% and 96% plus coverage 90/100 and 50/100.
Rejects ranking whole-population correctness from unequal survivor denominators; missingness rates do not establish independence/MAR.
Uses common sample IDs and matched paired analysis or explicit missingness/coverage sensitivity analysis; does not silently compare different survivors.

Separates observed correct-output yield 81/100 versus 48/100 (or bounds on unknown whole-population correctness) from unobserved correctness of failures; avoids declaring either method scientifically superior without defining reliability.
tasks.critical_failure: Declares missingness independent or whole-population accuracy superiority from survivors alone.

criteria: Identifies restart/search-budget confounding of the update-rule effect.
Rejects equal-cost claim: 20x restart budget and measured 1.4 versus 1.0 seconds; outer iteration cap is not total cost.
Proposes matched budgets or a method x restart factorial on common channels, reporting interaction/paired uncertainty.
Reports the observed 25 versus 23 (~8.7%) as the combined tested protocol gain and not a separately attributed update-rule benefit or universal speedup.
tasks.critical_failure: Attributes the gain solely to update rule or calls the costs equal.

criteria: Separates three AI pre-reviews from formal human/editorial reviews.
States only official Phase 2 advancement is confirmed and final acceptance is unknown.
Produces an accurate two-sentence progress statement without fabricated votes or reviewer identities.
Does not treat favorable reviews/phase advancement as proof of scientific correctness.
tasks.critical_failure: Claims final acceptance, three formal votes or proof of correctness.

criteria: Accepts the scoped Theta(b^-2) statement from the supplied two-sided bounds.
Uses positive constants independent of b, the same L/domain and b>=10 to justify the asymptotic definition.
Retains the wording under the stated assumptions as b tends to positive infinity.
Does not invent a missing lower bound, reject the statement merely because proofs are not reproduced, or extend it to algorithmic optimality/finite regimes.
tasks.critical_failure: Falsely rejects the supplied scoped Theta claim or asserts optimality of all algorithms.

criteria: Accepts the scoped observed-test result as consistent with the given design.
Recognizes train-only preprocessing, validation-only tuning and once-used frozen paired test do not exhibit the leakage described in T02.
Preserves +1 and [0.5,1.5] percentage-point interval, with tested-data scope and no universal/causal claim.

Suggests concrete reproduction details such as IDs/split seed, preprocessing/config/code, predictions or interval method without falsely declaring leakage, invalidity or demanding a full unrelated project.
tasks.critical_failure: Falsely declares test leakage/invalidity in the supplied design or asserts universal superiority.
